newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Two dead, 7 wounded in Burundi town fighting.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, 7 wounded in Burundi town fighting.

text.p: Two people died and seven were wounded in Burundi's southern Rumonge town on Saturday when Hutu rebels attacked a school bus in the latest incident in nearly two months fighting, eyewitnesses said.
Rebels have targeted the town in Bururi region on the east shore of Lake Tanganyika since April 27 with a series of ambushes and skirmishes with the army, residents said.

More than 600 rebels and and 65 civilians have died since fighting erupted in Rumonge and nearby communes, said Augustin Habonayo, political aide to Bururi's governor. Some 16,000 have been forced to flee their homes, he said.
There was no independent confirmation of the figures.

"There were 18 of us in the bus. When we crossed the Dama river at the north end of Rumonge town we heard gunfire, the vehicle turned over and I fell into the bushes," said Charlotte Haborimana, recovering in Rumonge hospital from bullet wounds.
"I want to ask the rebels to leave us in peace. But I don't know the words and nobody will listen, not even the military. In my opinion they should all let us get on with her lives," said Haborimana.

Fighting in Burundi's bitter ethnic civil war has swung south since last October when the armed wing of the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) was driven out of bases in East Zaire refugee camps.
Rebels, who attacked a transport lorry south of Rumonge on Thursday, want to "asphyxiate" the town, blocking all attempts at resupply, said Issa Rehani, a Rumonge businessman.
Burundi's military leader Pierre Buyoya, who took power last July in a coup, announced an agreement last month with CNDD aimed at producing a ceasefire.
More than 150,000 people have died in Burundi since the country's first freely-elected Hutu president was killed in an attempted coup by Tutsi troops.
